risks: Required paired seed injection and canonical stream mapping have unavailable evidence in the pinned sample, which lacks a seed CLI and uses device-derived streams. Unsupported adapter capabilities make evaluation invalid; identical stock runs cannot count as independent seeds.

Changing physical device assignment can change cuRAND streams unless canonical logical identities and path indices are preserved. Repartitioning can also alter floating-point reduction order, precision, or option ordering and thereby change scientific results.

The metric establishes only a median paired shift in mean standardized pricing error. It does not establish per-option equivalence or equivalence of error tails; aggregate cancellation can conceal option-specific changes.

The fixed margin is prospectively one baseline Monte Carlo standard error in normalized coordinates, not a published L1 tolerance. No empirical baseline paired variability is supplied, so the conditional power design provides no empirical power guarantee.

Host costs dominate much of the profile. Additional device initialization, duplicated state, dispatch, synchronization, gathering, or uneven option partitions may yield little speedup or a slowdown despite resource feasibility.

Packet does not establish existing baseline device usage or exact adapter paths. Already parallel baseline execution could leave less incremental benefit than the ideal sealed bound suggests; validate this later without changing the chosen method or protocol.
